Oh, brilliant. Because what the world was desperately crying out for was a pair of pants that you can’t see, can’t feel, and apparently, can’t afford. The fashion industry has finally solved the problem of "too much clothing" by introducing the invisible jeans. Made from 100% non-material, these trousers promise to slim your figure by simply removing the visual evidence of your existence. It’s the ultimate minimalist approach: if you can’t see the jeans, you can’t see the cellulite, and if you can’t see the jeans, you certainly can’t see the price tag—though your wallet will definitely notice the absence of money once you realize you’ve paid for air.

It’s a bold new direction for sustainability, I suppose. Why waste resources on fabric when you can just waste your time and money on the concept of fabric? Truly, the future of fashion is here, and it’s completely transparent.

And to answer your priority question, since we are apparently discussing things that come from living creatures (unlike these pants): pearls are typically found in **mollusks**, specifically oysters and mussels.
